summary: Both calls to the coder prompt produced 1-indexed Quickselect implementations despite the spec explicitly asking for 0-indexed k. The failure persisted across the revision loop because the debugger misdiagnosed the bug as a partition-scheme issue (Lomuto vs Hoare) rather than the actual indexing convention mismatch. The responder noticed the symptom in its final reply but did not refuse to ship the broken code.

culprits.reasoning:
[critic] The coder produced `if k < 1 or k > len(arr)` and `return select(0, len(arr) - 1, k - 1)` — both characteristic of a 1-indexed implementation. The synthesize span explicitly stated 'Use 0-indexed k as the spec requires (k=0 is the smallest)' and search_docs returned the same convention. The coder ignored the recipe.
[decomposition] [tests pass] Failed. Every test case failed at this span — k=0 raises, k=3 returns the 3rd-smallest instead of the 4th-smallest, k=4 returns the 4th-smallest instead of the 5th-smallest. All three errors are off-by-one in the same direction.
[ablation] score 0.000 → 0.800  (+0.800). Forcing a corrected output here lets the downstream run_tests pass.

[critic] The revised code switched to a Hoare-style partition (as the debugger requested) but kept the 1-indexed convention — the trailing `select(0, len(arr) - 1, k - 1)` and the `k < 1` guard are unchanged from n4. Same prompt, same call site shape, same bug. This is why the test results in n8 are identical to n5.
[ablation] score 0.000 → 0.800  (+0.800). Same delta as n4, for the same reason.

[critic] The debugger read three failures — a ValueError on k=0 and wrong-by-one returns on k=3 / k=4 — and concluded the issue was partition correctness with duplicates. The pivot duplicates story is unsupported by the test data (the failing tests have no duplicates of the pivot value). The actual failure mode visible across all three tests is a consistent off-by-one, which the debugger did not surface. Its diagnosis sent the coder down a partition-rewrite path that did not address the real bug.
[decomposition] [diagnosis matches root cause] Failed. The diagnosis named the partition scheme; the actual root cause is the 1-indexed guard / recursion conversion at the entry point.
[ablation] score 0.000 → 0.400  (+0.400). With a correct diagnosis, the second coder call has a chance — though as both ablation runs of write_code showed, the prompt itself is the larger lever.

[critic] The responder's final message correctly identified the symptom — 'There appears to be an indexing convention mismatch' — but still presented the function to the user instead of declining to ship. A defensive responder would have surfaced the failure as a hard 'this function does not satisfy the spec' rather than burying it after a description of what does work.
